title: Power Automate: self-healing repairs desktop flow selector failures with AI
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, preview licensing, prerequisites, admin paths and PowerShell command are supported by Microsoft sources. It reports the differences between Microsoft's articles rather than silently choosing one. The monitoring checklist names a control that is missing from the controls table.

claims.claim: The roadmap item is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The general availability target is March CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "March CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is April CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "April CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists the Desktop platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: Power Automate plans an agentic desktop-flow feature that uses AI to identify the intended element and generate an alternative selector after a selector fails.
claims.quote: When an existing selector can no longer locate the intended UI element, Power Automate for desktop uses AI to identify the element and generate an alternative selector.

claims.claim: The roadmap preview has an action-level opt-in for automatic recovery from selector errors.
claims.quote: The preview phase includes an action-level opt-in option for automatically trying to recover from a selector error

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: General availability is planned to add a flow-level opt-in that logs a working alternative selector without applying it at runtime.
claims.quote: the GA phase will additionally include a flow-level opt-in option to only log the alternative, working selector in case of an error, without applying the fix during runtime.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes self-healing as a preview with prerelease documentation subject to change.
claims.quote: [This topic is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet document the planned flow-level log-only option.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate self-healing pricing licensing meter limits general availability log-only; self-healing licensing credits log. Read self-healing, errors and build 2608; none describes the flow-level log-only option.

claims.claim: For a supported action failing with Element not found, error handling runs retry policy, self-healing, Set variable / Run subflow rules, then Continue flow run / Throw error.
claims.quote: Retry policy → Self-healing (preview) → 'Set variable / Run subflow' rules → Continue flow run / Throw error

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: A successful runtime repair is applied and the flow continues.
claims.quote: If the repair succeeds, the flow continues.

claims.claim: Normal error handling resumes if self-healing fails.
claims.quote: If it fails, normal error handling resumes.

claims.claim: Self-healing is runtime-only.
claims.quote: Self-healing is a runtime-only capability.

claims.claim: Self-healing applies to console and cloud runs, attended and unattended.
claims.quote: It applies to console and cloud (attended and unattended) runs

claims.claim: Self-healing has no effect during designer runs.
claims.quote: has no effect during designer runs.

claims.claim: The dedicated preview page limits support to specific UI and browser automation actions that interact with one UI element.
claims.quote: Is available only for specific UI and browser automation actions that interact with a single UI element

claims.claim: The dedicated self-healing page lists Element not found and Window not found errors.
claims.quote: Applies only to Element not found and Window not found errors.

claims.claim: Element not found errors are captured on primary and secondary screens.
claims.quote: Element not found errors are captured in both primary and secondary screens

claims.claim: Window not found errors are captured only when the window is found on the main screen.
claims.quote: Window not found errors are only captured when the window is found in the main screen.

claims.claim: The general error-handling article lists only Element not found errors for self-healing.
claims.quote: Self-healing is currently available only for specific UI and browser automation actions that interact with a single UI element, and applies only to Element not found errors.

claims.claim: The dedicated self-healing page excludes government clouds GCC, GCC High and DoD, and sovereign clouds.
claims.quote: Self-healing in Power Automate for desktop isn't currently available for use in government clouds (GCC, GCC High, DoD) or sovereign clouds.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: When invoked, self-healing captures a screenshot of the missing UI element.
claims.quote: If self-healing is enabled and invoked upon an error during runtime, Power Automate for desktop captures contextual information, including a screenshot of the missing UI element

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The captured context includes the parent window title.
claims.quote: the title of its parent window

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The captured context includes the full desktop image used to identify and recapture the intended element.
claims.quote: and the full desktop image, so that it can identify the most likely intended element and recapture its selector.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Self-healing currently uses GPT-4.1 mini and Claude Sonnet 4.5 together.
claims.quote: Two large language models are currently used in combination to power self-healing, GPT‑4.1 mini and Claude Sonnet 4.5.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The Power Automate portal does not currently show self-healing details in action-level run logs.
claims.quote: The Power Automate portal doesn't currently surface self-healing details in the action-level logs of the flow runs where self-healing was invoked.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Self-healing may occasionally identify an unintended UI element.
claims.quote: Because self-healing uses generative AI, it might occasionally identify an unintended UI element.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The repairWithAIInfo action-log property records repair attempts, their success or failure and the AI-generated selector used at runtime.
claims.quote: a new property called `repairWithAIInfo` displays if a repair attempt was made, whether it was successful or failed, and the AI-generated selector that was used at runtime.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The desktop flow run page has a self-healing summary with details from up to three successful attempts.
claims.quote: In the desktop flow run page, you can find a summary of the self-healing activity that corresponds to that specific run, including details from up to three successful self-healing attempts.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The preview is included for organization premium accounts at no extra cost.
claims.quote: Self-healing in Power Automate for desktop is currently available for organization premium accounts at no extra cost.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Preview usage may be subject to service limits or changes.
claims.quote: Usage might be subject to service limits or changes.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing specifically for self-healing general availability is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate self-healing pricing licensing meter limits general availability log-only; self-healing licensing credits log. Read self-healing and billing-questions; results covered preview entitlement and general Power Automate billing, not GA self-healing entitlement.

claims.claim: No self-healing-specific meter, credit rate or cap is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate self-healing pricing licensing meter limits general availability log-only; self-healing licensing credits log. Read self-healing, billing-questions and pay-as-you-go-meters search passages; none names a self-healing-specific meter, credit rate or cap.

claims.claim: Self-healing requires Power Automate for desktop version 2.66 or higher.
claims.quote: You need version 2.66 or higher for Power Automate for desktop.

claims.where: Scope; Risk assessment: Data exposure; summary
claims.claim: Self-healing requires Anthropic enabled as an organisational subprocessor in Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Self-healing relies on generative AI models and requires all of the following settings to be enabled

claims.where: Scope; Risk assessment: Data exposure; summary
claims.claim: Self-healing also requires Anthropic enabled at environment or environment group level in Power Platform.
claims.quote: expand External models and enable Anthropic as a subprocessor at environment or environment group level.

claims.where: Scope; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Self-healing requires Move data across regions selected where that checkbox is displayed.
claims.quote: Review the terms of use and select the Move data across regions checkbox.

claims.claim: The Move data across regions checkbox is neither displayed nor needed for US cloud regions.
claims.quote: The Move data across regions checkbox isn't displayed or needed for US cloud regions.

claims.claim: The general Copilot in Power Automate setting must be On for self-healing.
claims.quote: Under the Power Automate section, select Copilot in Power Automate, then enable the On check box in the displayed pane.

claims.claim: The dedicated self-healing page says it does not apply to window or screen handling actions.
claims.quote: Doesn't apply to window or screen handling actions

claims.claim: The dedicated page excludes multi-element actions such as Drag and drop UI element in window.
claims.quote: or actions that interact with multiple elements like 'Drag and drop UI element in window'.

claims.claim: Build 2608 release notes instead say self-healing also supports window manipulation actions.
claims.quote: Self-healing is now also supported for window manipulation actions in UI automation.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Anthropic reaches the organisational provider control.
claims.quote: In Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Settings, and then select AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors. Enable the Anthropic provider as a subprocessor for your organization.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Power Platform > External models > Anthropic reaches the environment provider setting.
claims.quote: In Power Platform admin center, go to Copilot > Settings, and then under the Power Platform section, expand External models and enable Anthropic as a subprocessor at environment or environment group level.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environment groups > environment group > Add rules > Power Platform Anthropic reaches the group rule checkbox.
claims.quote: select Environment groups, and then select the environment group. ... Select the Add rules tab. ... Select the checkbox for each rule that you want to add: Power Pages AI features, Power Platform Anthropic, Power Platform Mistral AI, or Power Platform XAI.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Generative AI features > Edit > Move data across regions reaches the data-movement control.
claims.quote: go to Manage > Environments. Select your environment so that you can see its details. In the Generative AI features card, select Edit. ... Review the terms of use and select the Move data across regions checkbox.

claims.claim: Set-PowerPlatformGenerativeAiSettings -EnvironmentName <environment-id> -CrossGeoDataMovement $true sets cross-region data movement in the named environment.
claims.quote: Set-PowerPlatformGenerativeAiSettings -EnvironmentName <String> [-CrossGeoDataMovement <Boolean>] ... -CrossGeoDataMovement: Enables or disables cross-geo data movement. ... -EnvironmentName: Specifies the ID of the environment you want to modify.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Power Automate > Copilot in Power Automate > On reaches the Copilot control.
claims.quote: In Power Platform admin center, go to Copilot > Settings. Under the Power Automate section, select Copilot in Power Automate, then enable the On check box in the displayed pane.

claims.claim: In the Power Automate for desktop designer, action > Error handling > Self-healing (Preview) reaches the per-action toggle.
claims.quote: Select a supported UI or browser automation action in the flow designer. ... Open the Error handling settings. ... Turn on Self-healing (Preview).

claims.claim: The provider's own guidance gives Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft 365 admin center and select Copilot > Settings > View all. ... Select AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors.

claims.claim: External models guidance alternatively places provider settings on Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environments, and then select the environment. ... select Settings. ... select Product > Features. ... turn each applicable model provider setting On or Off.

claims.claim: No documented API sets the Microsoft 365 Anthropic subprocessor control.
claims.quote: Searched: Anthropic AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors enable disable Microsoft Graph API PowerShell; Anthropic Graph subprocessor settings API. Read connect-to-ai-subprocessor and search results; no setting operation was documented.

claims.claim: No documented API sets the environment Anthropic model control.
claims.quote: Searched: Anthropic PowerShell Power Platform API environment settings. Read allow-llm-generative-responses, the environment-management settings tutorial and Update Environment Management Settings reference; no Anthropic setting property was documented.

claims.claim: No documented API sets the Power Platform Anthropic environment-group rule.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform Anthropic environment group rules API PowerShell. Read allow-llm-generative-responses, pac governance search passages and Rule Sets - Update Rule Set; generic rule operations exist, but no Anthropic rule identifier or deciding property was documented.

claims.claim: No public API operation is documented for the Copilot in Power Automate switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot in Power Automate tenant setting enable disable API PowerShell. Read copilot-overview and governance search passages; support-run PowerShell is mentioned, but no callable command or deciding parameter for this switch is published.

claims.claim: No API is documented for the individual action's self-healing toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate desktop self-healing action enable API Dataverse; Power Automate desktop self-healing Dataverse table entity reference enable. Read self-healing and table search passages; runtime-repair organisation fields do not document this per-action toggle.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Self-healing is user-opt-in: makers enable it per action after admin prerequisites are satisfied, with no source saying existing flows change automatically.
claims.quote: Enable self-healing per action: ... Turn on Self-healing (Preview). ... When enabled, the action can automatically retry by using AI when the element isn't found at runtime. Searched: Power Automate self-healing tenant environment disable switch.

claims.where: Scope; controls[0].note; controls[1].note; controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: A Microsoft 365 AI administrator enables the provider.
claims.quote: First, a Microsoft 365 AI administrator enables access to a model provider.

claims.claim: Environments in an environment group must be managed environments.
claims.quote: Environments in an environment group must be managed environments.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft enables Claude models by default for most commercial customers excluding EU/EFTA and UK.
claims.quote: Microsoft enables Claude models on by default for most customers in commercial cloud (excluding EU/EFTA and UK).

claims.claim: The checklist's self-healing monitoring control is not represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: Read the self-healing summary on the desktop flow run page and the repairWithAIInfo property in local action logs. Controls table: provider, environment models, group models, cross-region movement, Copilot and per-action enablement only.
claims.fix: The After rollout step that tells readers to read the desktop flow run summary and repairWithAIInfo logs has no monitoring row in the controls table; remove that checklist bullet to resolve the mismatch without adding a row.

claims.claim: A Power Platform system admin allows provider models in an environment or environment group.
claims.quote: Then, a Power Platform system admin allows the provider's models in an environment or environment group.

claims.claim: Apply changes publishes configured rules to environments in the group.
claims.quote: To publish the rules to the environments in the group, select Apply changes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Claude models deployed in Power Platform are excluded from EU Data Boundary and applicable in-country processing commitments.
claims.quote: Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings such as Microsoft Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary, and when applicable, in-country processing commitments.

claims.claim: The documented registry control is DWORD DisableRunFilesCleanup at HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Power Automate Desktop\Global, set to 1.
claims.quote: | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE | SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Power Automate Desktop\Global | DisableRunFilesCleanup | DWORD | ... 1: Flow run action details stored in the Actions.log file aren't deleted from the local disk after the run is completed.

claims.claim: Setting DisableRunFilesCleanup to 1 retains the local Actions.log action details after the run completes.
claims.quote: 1: Flow run action details stored in the Actions.log file aren't deleted from the local disk after the run is completed.

claims.where: Governance controls: The Learn page lists
claims.claim: No self-healing-specific administrator switch is documented, beyond the general model prerequisites and the maker's per-action toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate self-healing tenant environment disable switch; Power Automate desktop self-healing Dataverse table entity reference enable. Read self-healing and governance; table results describe runtime repair, not a switch identified as self-healing.
